results.fact: round-trip distance and gain figures disagree
results.evidence: External figures for this same climbers' path do not converge: one hike listing gives 7.0 mi RT / 3,500 ft; a GPS trip report (author warns of multipath errors) gives 7.4 mi / 3,913 ft; a mapping-app listing gives 5.3 mi RT / 3,911 ft; another listing gives 4.62 mi / 3,556 ft. No two independent sources agree on one distance, and the sister South Route row (same path) itself stores 5.3 mi with waypoints ending at 2.65 mi. Left open rather than picking a side.

results.fact: climb length (length_m) appears to include the non-technical approach
results.evidence: The first-ascent account describes a 3,500-ft north face whose lower ~2,000-2,300 ft is steep brush and forest (Couloir Camp ~1,000 ft above the lake, Dolomite Camp ~2,300 ft above it), topped by four rock steps of 300, 400, 220 and 250 ft. length_m 1067 m = 3,500 ft is the whole face (about 2,300 ft of brushy lower face plus 1,170 ft of steps), which is what the approach and pitch_detail fields together describe. Another reference also calls it a ~3,000-ft wall.

results.fact: access.fees claims no fee, other access fields require a pass/fee
results.correct_value: Day-use fee at the Barclay Lake trailhead: $5 per vehicle per day or $30 annual, covered by a Northwest Forest Pass or an Interagency pass. There is no separate climbing fee.
results.evidence: The Forest Service trailhead page lists a $5 per vehicle day fee or $30 annual, honouring the Northwest Forest Pass, digital passes and Interagency passes (Discover Pass not valid). The hike listing for Mount Baring from this trailhead also states an America the Beautiful or Northwest Forest Pass is required. So 'None' in access.fees is wrong.

results.fact: turnaround implies a rappel descent; descent fields say it's a walk-off
results.correct_value: Standard descent is the non-technical walk-off down the south/west side and the climbers' path; rappels only on a mid-face retreat.
results.evidence: descent, descent_text, the summit waypoint note and directions, the timing sectionBreakdown and itinerary day 2 all describe a walk-off, against turnaround alone. A 2013 north-face ascent report describes going down an extremely steep trail to the valley after topping out, i.e. the climbers' path, not rappels. The 1960 first-ascent party did rappel the upper walls, but in fog before the walk-off was known, which descent_text already frames as history/contingency.

patches.fact: turnaround implies a rappel descent; descent fields say it's a walk-off
patches.find: to ensure safe rappel descent before dark. Stopping early is critical given the complex multi-rope rappel descent required.
patches.replace: so the walk-off down the south side and the steep climbers' path can be finished before dark. Stopping early matters most if the party has to retreat off the face, because that means slow rappels from natural anchors.

results.fact: '1-14' pitch entry's stated face height vs its own numeric length
results.evidence: The only published record gives a 2,600-ft north face, about 14 pitches, 5.11c, Grade V. The 2,600 ft is the face height, and the row splits that face into ~305 m of brushy lower face (pitch_detail[0]) plus 488 m of pitches (pitch_detail[1]): 305 + 488 = 793 m, about 2,600 ft, which also equals length_m 792. The figures are consistent; the note labels the face, not the pitch sum.

dist_km 5.6 km (3.5 mi one way) matches a 7.0 mi RT hike listing and a 7.4 mi GPS report; the itinerary/variant 5.3 mi RT (2.65 mi one way) matches a mapping-app listing; another listing gives 4.62 mi RT. External sources split, so neither value is settled; the Northwest Ridge row (same path) carries the same open question and both should be settled together.

results.fact: rope_note claims a 5th-class crux; grade fields cap the route at Class 3-4
results.correct_value: Crux is a short, exposed Class 3-4 step on the summit block
results.evidence: Independent descriptions rate the standard route an easy class-3 scramble (an encyclopedia entry drawn from the regional climbing literature; a scramble-guide page calling it Class 3 with easy scrambling to the north summit; another listing calling the top 600 ft grade-3 scrambling). results.fact: Which line the route actually climbs (West Ridge crest vs. a different 'Southeast Slopes' gully)
results.correct_value: The summit day climbs the West Ridge: east from Holden Pass along the Bonanza-Martin ridge to the saddle at the ridge's foot, then gullies on the south side of the crest.
results.evidence: A detailed Holden Pass route description says to go east from Holden Pass over two small bumps on the ridge connecting Bonanza and Martin to a saddle at the base of Martin's West Ridge, traverse right onto the south side into a deep loose gully, exit on Class 3-4 rock just below its overhang, then link gullies south of the crest for the last 1,000 ft. A separate trip report likewise climbs from Holden Pass to a notch in the west ridge, then Class 3-4 on the crest and ribs/gullies including a beige-marble gully. So the itinerary's gully IS the West Ridge line; only the 'Southeast Slopes' name and 'toward Bonanza' (Bonanza is west; the travel is east) are wrong.

results.fact: Whether Martin Peak has a drive-to trailhead requiring a self-issue permit
results.evidence: The permit field states a wilderness permit rule; it does not claim a drive-in trailhead. Martin lies in the Glacier Peak Wilderness and the Railroad Creek trailhead at Holden Village is a real (boat-and-shuttle-reached) trailhead; a trip report notes wilderness permits apply. The 2025-26 FSR 8301 closure (confirmed closed through 2026) is a temporary access closure, separate from the permit rule, and access.permit null is an absence, not a counter-claim. The generic 'Northwest Forest Pass at many trailheads' clause could not be confirmed for Holden either way.

results.fact: access.permit says 'None required' but the top-level permit field says a free self-issue Wild Sky Wilderness permit or trailhead registration
results.evidence: Could not find an official statement of whether the Wild Sky Wilderness uses self-issue permits; the forest's wilderness-regulations material surfaced self-issue permits for Alpine Lakes but nothing for Wild Sky. The sister Northwest Ridge row says no permit. Left open.

results.evidence: An encyclopedia entry gives 8,509 ft; a detailed trip report gives 8,511 ft and another cites 8,511/8,504. The small split reflects differing surveys/datums; no two independent sources were found agreeing against the other.

results.fact: distance and gain: dist_km 25.75 km (16 mi, shown as the one-way approach) and gain_ft 5300 vs itinerary days 7 + 3.5 + 7 mi and 3,200 + 2,200 = 5,400 ft gain, and totalNote '~16 mi and ~5,400 ft round trip'
results.evidence: dist_km appears to hold a round-trip total rather than a one-way approach, and gain_ft (5,300) differs from the itinerary sum (5,400). One trip report gives 12 mi and 5,600 ft round trip from Holden Village. No second agreeing source for a specific figure, so left open.
